name: Mast Cell Leukemia

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO Diagnostic Criteria for Mast Cell Leukemia

criteria.description: Bone marrow biopsy showing ≥20% atypical mast cells
Peripheral blood mast cells ≥10% of leukocytes
Presence of activating KIT mutation (commonly D816V)
Atypical or immature mast cell morphology on cytology

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of ≥20% mast cells in bone marrow and ≥10% mast cells in peripheral blood
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of other myeloid neoplasms and confirmation of mast cell lineage.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Circulating atypical mast cells in peripheral blood
searchTerms: atypical mast cells detected in bloodstream

pathognomonic.symptomName: Bone marrow infiltration by neoplastic mast cells
searchTerms: bone marrow filled with abnormal mast cells
low red blood cells from marrow disease
anemia caused by bone marrow problems
reduced blood counts due to marrow infiltration

common.symptomName: Flushing episodes related to mast cell mediator release

searchTerms: general feeling of illness with weight loss

occasional.symptomName: Bone pain due to marrow expansion

searchTerms: digestive pain and frequent bowel movements

occasional.symptomName: Pruritus related to mast cell degranulation

rare.symptomName: Neurological symptoms due to CNS mast cell infiltration
searchTerms: neurological problems from mast cells in brain
nerve symptoms due to brain mast cell involvement
CNS symptoms from mast cell infiltration

rare.symptomName: Cardiovascular hypotension and shock from mast cell mediator release
searchTerms: low blood pressure and shock from allergic mediators
cardiovascular collapse during mast cell activation
shock caused by mast cell chemicals

rare.symptomName: Renal impairment secondary to mast cell infiltration
searchTerms: kidney problems from mast cell buildup
renal impairment due to cell infiltration
kidney damage related to mast cells

laboratory: Peripheral blood smear showing ≥10% atypical mast cells
Bone marrow biopsy with ≥20% mast cell infiltration
Anemia and thrombocytopenia on complete blood count
imaging: Hepatosplenomegaly on abdominal ultrasound or CT
Lytic bone lesions on skeletal survey or MRI
genetic: Activating KIT mutation, commonly D816V detected by molecular testing
other: Flow cytometry showing aberrant mast cell immunophenotype (CD25+, CD2+)
Histopathology demonstrating atypical mast cell morphology

distinguishingFeatures: Lower mast cell burden (<20% in marrow)
Absence or low percentage of circulating mast cells
Presence of >20% mast cells but with acute leukemia features
Predominance of myeloblasts with some mast cell features

redFlags: High peripheral blood mast cell count (>10%)
references: Arber DA, et al. The 2016 revision to the WHO classification of myeloid neoplasms and acute leukemia. Blood. 2016.
Valent P, et al. Mast cell leukemia: 2021 update on diagnosis, risk stratification, and management. Leukemia. 2021.
